t: The provisions of title II of the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act (42 U.S.C. 11311 et seq.) shall continue in effect, notwithstanding section 209 of such Act, through the earlier of: (1) the date specified in section 106(3) of this division; or (2) the date of the enactment into law of an authorization Act relating to the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act.

fable.w: This section only extends the sunset date of title II of the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act; it sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. The tempting reading is that the extended title (which concerns the Interagency Council on Homelessness) may involve outside coordination, but nothing in this section's own text recommends or requires any outside-party involvement in a federal decision.
fable.s: shall continue in effect, notwithstanding section 209 of such Act

qwen_block.w: This section is a continuation of authority provision, extending the legal effect of existing statutes until a future date or legislative action. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) regarding a federal decision. It merely defines the temporal scope of existing law.
qwen_block.s: The provisions of title II of the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act (42 U.S.C. 11311 et seq.) shall continue in effect, notwithstanding section 209 of such Act, through the earlier of: (1) the date specified in section 106(3) of this division; or (2) the date of the enactment into law of an authorization Act relating to the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act.

opus.w: This is a continuing-appropriations provision. It only keeps an existing title in force until a set date or until a new authorization act is passed. It sets up no comment period, hearing, outside advisory body, consultation with non-federal parties, or right to sue. Title II deals with an interagency council of federal agencies, so even reading the referenced title into the section would only bring in coordination inside the federal government.
opus.s: The provisions of title II of the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act (42 U.S.C. 11311 et seq.) shall continue in effect, notwithstanding section 209 of such Act
opus.b:
1. **Reasoning:** The tempting reading is "Yes", because Title II of the McKinney-Vento Act sets up the Interagency Council on Homelessness, a coordinating body. That fails for two reasons. The section itself only extends a sunset date by cross-reference, and it says nothing about consulting anyone. And the Council is made up of federal agencies, so any coordination it does stays inside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: This section merely extends the effective date of another statute. It does not create any new requirement for consultation, public comment, hearings, or advisory committees. It involves no interaction with outside parties regarding a federal decision, but rather defines the temporal scope of existing legal authority.
qwen_chat.s: The provisions of title II of the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act (42 U.S.C. 11311 et seq.) shall continue in effect, notwithstanding section 209 of such Act, through the earlier of: (1) the date specified in section 106(3) of this division; or (2) the date of the enactment into law of an authorization Act relating to the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the section references the "McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act," which contains provisions for public participation (like comment periods for local plans), this section implicitly requires participation. However, this section itself is merely a continuation of existing law's validity; it does not establish, require, or describe any specific participatory process. It is a procedural provision regarding the lifespan of a statute, not a mandate for public input.
